title: The Dancing Plague of 1518: Did It Really Kill 15 People a Day?
description:
In 1518, hundreds of people in Strasbourg danced for days and could not stop. Almost every retelling claims the dancing plague killed fifteen people a day — but the city's own records from that summer tell a different story.

In this documentary we follow the epidemic from Frau Troffea's first steps to the shrine of Saint Vitus, look at why the city's "cure" made everything worse, separate documented fact from later legend, and explore why historians now believe this was a mass psychogenic illness born from famine, fear and faith.

Sources:
- John Waller, The Dancing Plague: The Strange, True Story of an Extraordinary Illness (2009)
- John Waller, "A forgotten plague: making sense of dancing mania", The Lancet (2009)

Subscribe for more of history's darkest mysteries — told carefully, with the sources.
